recipes.name: Good New Orleans Creole Gumbo
ingredients_raw: 1 large green bell pepper, coarsely chopped
2 tablespoons hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®), or to taste
0.5 teaspoon Cajun seasoning blend (such as Tony Chachere's®), or to taste
2 (10 ounce) packages frozen cut okra, thawed
3 pounds uncooked medium shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: Make the roux: Whisk together flour and 3/4 cup bacon drippings in a large, heavy saucepan over medium-low heat until smooth. Cook roux, whisking constantly, until it turns a rich mahogany brown color. This can take 20 to 30 minutes; watch heat carefully and whisk constantly or roux will burn. Remove from heat; continue whisking until mixture stops cooking.
Make the gumbo: Place celery, onion, green bell pepper, and garlic into the work bowl of a food processor, and pulse until all vegetables are very finely chopped.
Stir vegetables into roux, and mix in sliced sausage. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until vegetables are tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Combine water and beef bouillon cubes in a large Dutch oven or soup pot and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Stir until bouillon cubes dissolve, then whisk roux mixture into the boiling water.

Reduce heat to a simmer and mix in sugar, salt, hot pepper sauce, Cajun seasoning, bay leaves, thyme, stewed tomatoes, and tomato sauce. Simmer soup over low heat for 1 hour; mix in 2 teaspoons of file gumbo powder at the 45-minute mark.
Meanwhile, melt 2 tablespoons bacon drippings in a skillet over medium heat. Add okra and vinegar and cook for 15 minutes; remove okra with a slotted spoon, and stir into the simmering gumbo.
Mix in crabmeat, shrimp, and Worcestershire sauce, and simmer until flavors have blended, 45 more minutes. Stir in 2 more teaspoons of file gumbo powder just before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Good New Orleans Creole Gumbo
raw_recipe.description: Traditional Creole gumbo made with roux, shrimp, sausage, and crabmeat. Delicious served over hot cooked rice.

review.reviewBody: You should be ashamed of yourself. Family recipes are suppose to be just that, kept in the family. But I'm fo sho glad you shared this one. This is what gumbo is suppose to be.Just the right amount of kick but not to spicy. This will now be passed on down to my family. Thanks Doc!!!

I was looking for an authentic gumbo recipe and I found it. I've cooked for a long time and try to follow a recipe exactly the first time I make it. As is, this is a great recipe! I did add a little more Cajun seasoning and cayenne pepper the next day since we like things with "heat". My wife said that I outdid myself. Thank you dailyrecipedoctor and your mother and grandmother.
My family's favorite gumbo. It's fabulous over rice, but if you add two or three cups of water you've got the best thick soup type gumbo you'll ever taste.

I have been using this recipe for YEARS and people swear I have New Orleans heritage (lol). The recipe as written is AMAZING but I made a few modifications to enhance this masterpiece.Place 2 pounds of chicken breast in a pressure cooker with 3 cups of water and cook until done (about 40 minutes).Place cooked chicken in a stockpot and add ANY COMBINATION of (10) CUPS of Seafood STOCK and Chicken STOCK. I usually use (4) cups (32 ounces) SEAFOOD STOCK and (6) cups (48 OUNCES) CHICKEN STOCK. NOTE: You may substitute Chicken BROTH for chicken STOCK. I find using the STOCK instead of water gives the gumbo a richer flavor. I hope you find this tip useful….ENJOY!
Loved this recipe but I would add the shrimp like 10 minutes before it's done and not boil them for 45 min.

The shrimp should not go in with 45 minutes of cook time remaining. Last 10 minutes is plenty & won't overcook the shrimp. Also, I used Better than Bullion brand Lobster bullion & Roaster Garlic bullion instead of the over-salted beef bullion cubes. The combination added excellent flavor.

Having spent many years in Louisiana I cooked many Cajun dishes. I was looking for a good Creole for style gumbo and happened on this recipe. I followed it pretty much to a T, with the exception of not cooking the shrimp 45 minutes. Please please please don't cook your shrimp. Just make sure the gumbo is piping hot and place the shrimp in. By the time you plate up your rice, The shrimp are done to perfection! Using bacon fat in a roux has never occurred to me. It is brilliant! This recipe is absolutely positively outstanding. I had some dear friends come over and everyone commented on how good the gumbo was. I felt like a New Orleans chef. If you want the best gumbo in my opinion, this is the one!

2 days of searching for File seasoning, 5 hours of cooking , but I don't think I'll have to go back to New Orleans. I had to substitute 1/2 cup of butter because I ran out of bacon fat for the Roux. The Roux took me 45 minutes I was afraid of burning the Roux. I grabbed a stool, my iPad, glass of wine, and stirred nonstop. I was able to get the Roux to a milky chocolate. I just sample the complete product , it's incredible. I can't imagine what it will taste like later and I can't wait to drown my portion with some Crystal hot sauce! Thank you

Some have said this is not an authentic Louisianagumbo because it includes tomato and okra. New Orleans gumbo includes tomatoes and okra. In other parts of Louisiana, they may not use those. I was born and raised in New Orleans and this is an authentic recipe, except we chop the vegetables and don’t purée them. We sauté them instead.
This was really good but I think simmering your shrimp for 45 minutes way overcooks them. Next time I’m going to put them in the last 5-10 minutes.

This gumbo taste just like the Gumbo my Grandmother used to make. I followed the recipe with one exception. I boiled the shells from the shrimp then strained and added the beef bullion cubes to that water. The flavor is kicking good! Love it! Thank you so much!
I made this gumbo recipe today. Glad to report that is was worth all the effort as my wonderful boyfriend loved it.
I made this recipe and all my guest loved it

I've been using this recipe since at least 2011, and probably longer. The ONLY thing I've ever changed are as follows: I double the Creole seasoning, I wait until the last half hour to add the shrimp, I also add 1-1/2 pounds of chicken to it, with all other ingredients remaining the same.

Followed the recipe minus the okra...lived in Louisiana for a while and never got used to it no matter how it was prepared. I had a small serving of the gumbo immediately after it was done and can say this is AMAZING. I didn't think it would have enough heat but it did (I used The Original Louisiana Hot Sauce -- found in most stores). So flavorful! Can't wait to try it tomorrow to see if it tastes even better than perfect! I did add about 3 Cups of cooked white rice into the entire pot at the very end.

This is a very good recipe. Very close to my grandmothers Gumbo. I just remove most of the seeds from the okra because we don't like the slim and removing the seeds helps with this. I also cut the okra amount about 50%. Also, NO WAY would we cook the shrimp for that long. 15 minutes at the most and 10 minutes if they are small. Judy in NOLA

This is the most delicious dish I have ever made! Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe. The only changes I made was to leave out the crab meat…although I may try this recipe with crab meat next time!

I've been using Paul Prudhomme's seafood gumbo recipe for over 30 years. It does not call for a roux but margarine instead. It is the best gumbo I've ever had. NOTE: I've eaten gumbo in New Orleans, and it's great, but not better than Paul's.

I did not use crab meat. I did saute 4 boneless skinless chicken thighs and de-glazed the pan with the tomatoes, I used only 1 pkg of Okra only 1 pound of shrimp. I think I would cut the water down to 2 qts and I did thicken with a cornstarch slurry. I had no File' (Nor did my grocer).
Number one tweak NO OKRA! I HATE slimy Okra! I replaced with Brussel sprouts peeled and cut in half...MUCH better and gives a nice cabbage taste instead.
